evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Vindobona: Vindobona, Vendobona, Vindomana, Vindomina, Juliobona, Flaviana castra, Vienna, Vienna Austriae od. Fluviorum … Wien
terms.comment: The name of the Roman town on the Danube. Lewis & Short has no entry for it, but Aurelius Victor, in the fourth century, writes Vendobona (Caes. 16.14), so it is labelled late. A town takes no preposition: Vindobonam (to), Vindobonae (in, at), Vindobonā (from).

evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Vindobona: Vindobona, Vendobona, Vindomana, Vindomina, Juliobona, Flaviana castra, Vienna, Vienna Austriae od. Fluviorum … Wien
terms.comment: The later name, closer to the modern one; Morgan–Owens finds it a little more common in printed books. The classical Vienna is Vienne on the Rhône (Lewis & Short).
